speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) when did LTA start requiring new Taxi Driver's Vocational Licence applicants to have a GCE "O" or "N" level pass in English or at least a Level 3 pass in the Listening, Reading and Speaking modules of the Workplace Literacy-Computer Adaptive Test; and (b) why does LTA require experienced taxi drivers who had their licences revoked and are applying afresh for a vocational licence to also meet this requirement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The Workplace Literacy assessment could be completed in about two hours.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: But they would have great difficulty passing a two-hour English and math test.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Has the Ministry considered that this Workplace Literacy test requirement may present an insurmountable hurdle for taxi drivers, especially these experienced taxi drivers who do not possess the educational qualifications?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Can it consider doing away with this test requirement for older, experienced drivers?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, by 1979, the Registry of Vehicles had introduced an oral English proficiency assessment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Prior to that, in place of relevant certificates, they could attend an oral English assessment interview.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, if their licence is revoked and they want to get back the licence, they will have to apply as a fresh applicant.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Therefore, we require them to fulfil all the prevailing requirements, including English language proficiency.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Having said that, because this requirement has been in place for such a long time, most of the TDVL licence holders would have already fulfilled this requirement and all they need to show is documentary proof that they have fulfilled the requirement.
